fixes.explanation: That's the job, baker. David and the commanders set these sons apart "…to prophesy with the accompaniment of lyres, harps, and cymbals." (1 Chronicles 25:1) So the assignment is prophesying, and instruments go right along with it. I love that.

Nope, no treasury shifts here. The text says they were set apart to prophesy with lyres, harps and cymbals (1 Chronicles 25:1). Cymbals are LOUD. Picture a guard crashing cymbals every time he turns a corner, and the whole night shift hears him coming.

That's it, baker. The text says Jeduthun "…prophesied with the harp, giving thanks and praise to the LORD." (1 Chronicles 25:3) Thanks and praise, with a harp in his hands. I think that's a fine way to spend a day.
I see why you'd guess that, but this verse says Jeduthun prophesied with the harp "…giving thanks and praise to the LORD." (1 Chronicles 25:3) Nothing about enemies here. This one's all thanks.

Careful, friend, those two are opposites. The text says the sons were given to Heman "…through the promises of God to exalt him…" (1 Chronicles 25:5) Exalt means lift up, not bring down. So this is a gift, not a lesson in humility.
